$comment: Tier divergences the vertical gate has FOUND and that are not yet fixed.
An entry here does not make a divergence acceptable — it makes it tracked.
The runner treats a listed (tier, case) pair as KNOWN rather than FAIL, and
then fails in the other direction: an entry whose divergence no longer
reproduces is stale and must be deleted in the same commit that fixes the
bug. Any divergence NOT listed here fails the suite outright.
Adding an entry requires the exact bytes and a fund-safety assessment, so
'allowlist it' costs about as much as reading the bug.
expectedFirstDiff is REQUIRED for every listed case (the runner throws at
load time otherwise): { byte, golden, tier }, all derived from the
checked-in expected-code-part.hex vs. the tier's actual bytes. 'golden' is
the byte the independent derivation says belongs at that offset; 'tier' is
the byte the DIVERGENT TIER actually produces there (not the tier's name —
the tier name is already the entry's top-level 'tier' field). A listed
(tier, case) pair is classified KNOWN only when its divergence reproduces
this EXACT byte; any other divergence on that pair (a different byte, a
truncated/empty result) is NEW and fails the suite outright — see
vertical-runner.ts's knownFor().
Previously listed here: 'ruby-scriptnum-minus-one' (Ruby encoded a bigint
-1 constructor/method arg as the direct push '0181' instead of OP_1NEGATE
'4f'). Fixed in packages/runar-rb/lib/runar/sdk/state.rb — the entry
stopped reproducing (the runner's stale-entry gate caught it) and was
deleted in the same change that landed the fix.
